events.what: Joshi claims Arithmetic Teichmuller Spaces plus Mochizuki's IUT completes a proof of abc and that the Scholze-Stix objections fail (preprint series with 2025 FAQ and report)
events.credibility_reason: F5: restates a decade-old dispute rather than advancing it; the relevant experts (Scholze and others) remain unconvinced; no uptake or acceptance after 2.5 years on a landmark problem; the 2026 LANA formalisation project explicitly declines to endorse IUT as a proof; a 2026 fact-check rates 'abc has been proven' False. JUDGE.md names this exact claim as an F5 example.

events.what: Bernert, Browning, Lichtman and Teravainen bound the number of abc exceptional triples in a cube of side N by O(N^(33/50)), improving the 1962 O(N^(2/3)) bound
LANA (ZEN University) Lean formalisation project interim report on IUT, withholding judgement

judgement.doubts: The researcher kept Joshi's claim only because the old rule made any undigested preprint 'claimed'; its own competing_reading gives the F5 signals. The exceptional-set bound is a count of exceptions, not finiteness, so it is a bound, not a case. The researcher dismissed it as 'instances' by analogy, but it bounds a quantity for all N and is not a finite check. 2505.13991 is a related density paper and does not change the tier.

outcome_prefix: Bernert, Browning, Lichtman and Teräväinen (arXiv 2410.12234, October 2024) improved the bound on abc exceptional triples in a cube of side N from O(N^(2/3)) to O(N^(33/50)); Joshi's claimed proof is set aside as not credible.

corrections.why: F5: the record's competing_reading gives the signals itself: Joshi's claim 'largely restates a 2012-2021 dispute', Scholze remains unconvinced, there is no acceptance after more than two years, and LANA withholds judgement. It is set aside as not credible. The surviving event is the O(N^(33/50)) exceptional-set bound in the summary, which is progress.
